WHY IT EXISTS. Verification on this board is CONCENTRATED, not smeared: mid-epic rows prove their own slice with focused tests and move on, and ONE row at the end gates the whole. The four band parents named in dependsOn (f3edb8fb Gate 2, 2a345b2e Gate 3, e7a20a49 control room, 8a6d6660 design) are each integration-shaped for their OWN band. Nothing in this epic currently tests what the bands got wrong ABOUT EACH OTHER, and that is exactly where this epic's risk lives, because all four bands write to the same shared roster files.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS - the four things no single slice could see:

1. THE SHARED ROSTER IS WHOLE. `preview.decide`, `release.decide`, `design.submit` and `design.read` each landed through packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts, its hand-transcribed runtime-contract.test.ts, the regenerated control-room client, and the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors. Assert the end state is coherent: the runtime roster, the daemon PAYLOAD_KEYS served set, the registry, and the generated client agree in BOTH directions (global rail 9), and every digest mirror carries the CURRENT hex. The bidirectional set-equality is the point - a subset check passes while a served capability has silently vanished from the advertised surface.

2. THE THREE HUMAN GATES COMPOSE ON ONE GOAL. Gate 1 (product contract), the design step, Gate 2 (working preview) and Gate 3 (release) are four decisions in one operator's sequence. Prove the sequence end to end on a single goal against a real store: approve the contract, submit or SKIP a design, approve the preview, approve the release. That flow does not exist to be tested until every band has landed - which is what makes it this row's and not any slice's.

3. THE HUMAN-ONLY FENCE HOLDS ACROSS ALL FOUR KINDS AT ONCE. Every gate kind must be operator-principal-only, MCP-excluded, and in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS. Each band asserted its own; assert the SET. Enumerate the served kinds from the dispatch seam and assert that every gate kind is fenced on all three axes - a kind added to two of the three rosters is exactly the defect class that minted 8 junk goals live.

4. THE DOCS SWEEP for this epic, held back from the individual rows so the same file is not re-edited five times.

THE HUMAN-ONLY FENCE HOLDS FOR THE WHOLE SET AT ONCE (DoD 4). Write `apps/daemon/src/gates-human-only-fence.test.ts`.

Enumerate the gate kinds from the IMPLEMENTATION SEAM (the served registry keys filtered to this epic's kinds), not from a hand list, so a kind added to two of the three rosters cannot pass by being absent from the list the test iterates. For EVERY gate kind, assert ALL THREE AXES TOGETHER:
1. OPERATOR-PRINCIPAL-ONLY — present in `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:355).
2. MCP-EXCLUDED — absent from `wiredMcpToolKinds()`. Assert against that function, which computes the actual served-over-MCP surface (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:81), not against the exclusion roster: the exclusion list is DERIVED from `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` (:78), so asserting it against axis 1 would be circular and would pass with the fence broken.
3. HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS — present in the set at agent-spawn-contract.ts:195. Note this is ONE Set re-exported by agent-wrapper.ts, NOT a byte-for-byte duplicate; several task descriptions on this board still claim otherwise and that claim is stale.

A kind fenced on two of three axes is the defect class this arm exists for — it is what minted 8 junk goals live — so assert the three together per kind and report which axis failed, not merely that one did.

Then the REFUSAL: dispatch each gate kind with an AGENT-authenticated principal and assert the specific stable reason CODE and the LAYER that refused. Never merely that it failed — a test asserting only "refused" is one added layer away from vacuous, because a second refusal layer can answer first and the arm stays green while no longer testing its subject. Mutate the fence and confirm the arm reds.

  2. MCP-EXCLUDED - asserted as `!new Set(wiredMcpToolKinds()).has(kind)`, i.e. against the ACTUAL served-over-MCP surface (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:99). THE INVARIANT IS ALL-THREE-OR-NONE-OF-THREE, PER KIND, and it is stronger than "the human gates are fenced". It catches a kind fenced on TWO axes - the leak that minted 8 junk goals live - WITHOUT the test needing to know in advance which side of the line a new kind belongs on. The assertion is written as `expect({...axes, fenced}).toEqual({...axes, fenced: fenced === 0 ? 0 : 3})`, so a failure prints the whole axis record and NAMES WHICH AXIS DISAGREED rather than merely that one did.

MEASURED AXES AT HEAD (tsx probe against the production surfaces, probe deleted in the same command):

  preview.start    op=true  mcpExcluded=true  humanOnly=true    3/3
  release.decide   op=true  mcpExcluded=true  humanOnly=true    3/3
  design.submit    op=false mcpExcluded=false humanOnly=false   0/3
`design.submit` AT 0/3 IS CORRECT AND IS ASSERTED AS SUCH, not tolerated. daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:200-217 states that copying the human-only shape onto the design step would leave every roster test in the repo green while making the step PERMANENTLY UNSTAFFABLE - the chain would simply never advance. A blanket three-axis assertion over the whole band would therefore have been WRONG, not strict, and would have pressured a future editor into breaking the design lane for "consistency". There is a dedicated arm pinning design.submit at exactly 0/3, so a tidy-up that fenced it reds here.

THE HUMAN FLOOR IS A FLOOR, and I state its limit rather than overclaiming. `HUMAN_GATE_FLOOR = [preview.decide, preview.start, release.decide]` is a hand list, but it can only FAIL CLOSED: removing a fence from a shipped gate reds it, and no sibling row bumping a roster can move it. It does not catch a brand-new band kind landing unfenced on all three axes (that satisfies the invariant); the floor is what a later row extends, and the refusal arms below are what prove the fence is real rather than declared. There is also an arm asserting every floor gate is actually SERVED by the registry, so a gate that vanished cannot silently drop out of every sweep and take its coverage with it.

THE REFUSAL NAMES ITS CODE AND ITS LAYER, AND THE CAPABILITY LAYER CANNOT ANSWER FIRST. For each floor gate the arm opens an AGENT session holding EXACTLY `registry.get(kind).requiredCapability` - read from the production entry, not transcribed - so AUTHORIZE passes and the OPERATOR fence is the layer that answers. A weaker session would have refused CAPABILITY_DENIED @ AUTHORIZE and the arm would have been green while the human fence was gone; that is the "one added layer away from vacuous" failure, and it is designed out. Routing is by `entry.asyncHandler === undefined`: preview.decide is SYNC (registry -> runPreviewDecideEdge), preview.start and release.decide are ASYNC entries that bypass the registry's synchronous fence and fence themselves at handler entry. All three answer the SAME pair, asserted exactly:
  { code: "OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED", layer: "DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION" }
and the sweep asserts `seen` equals the whole floor, so it cannot short-circuit after the first kind and still pass.
POSITIVE CONTROL in the same describe: the same machinery dispatches `design.submit` on a seat session and asserts its refusal code is NOT the operator code - it reaches its own slice instead.
